meta.title: IQE plc — Compound-semiconductor epitaxy at the AI-photonics and 5G-RF inflection
meta.abstract: IQE plc is the world's leading independent supplier of compound semiconductor epitaxial wafers, the precursor material on which gallium arsenide, indium phosphide, gallium nitride, and silicon-germanium devices are built. Listed on the London Stock Exchange AIM market (AIM:IQE), the company supplies wafers used in 5G RF power amplifiers, fibre-optic transceivers, VCSEL 3D-sensing arrays for smartphones, automotive LiDAR, and increasingly the optical-interconnect layer of AI data centres. Headquartered in Cardiff, Wales with major US operations in Pennsylvania (Bethlehem) and Massachusetts (Taunton), plus operations in Singapore and Taiwan. The 2024-2026 period has been defined by a CEO transition, sustained losses on the smartphone VCSEL cycle reset, and the emerging InP photonics demand pull from AI data centre optical interconnect.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
IQE plc occupied a position in the compound semiconductor supply chain for which there was no credible merchant-scale substitute. The Cardiff-headquartered company was the world's leading independent supplier of compound semiconductor epitaxial wafers — the precisely grown III-V and II-VI semiconductor layer-stacks on which gallium arsenide radio-frequency amplifiers, indium phosphide optical transceivers, gallium nitride power devices and VCSEL arrays were subsequently fabricated. Without IQE's reactor halls running product, the merchant compound semiconductor supply chain ceased to function at scale. That structural reality both defined the company's strategic value and underscored the urgency of the financial problems that accumulated through 2022–2025.

Founded in Cardiff, Wales in 1988, IQE grew from Epitaxial Products International into what the company described as the scaled global epitaxy leader, with manufacturing and substrate operations across the UK, the US and Taiwan [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/) [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). By 31 December 2024, the group employed 479 people [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf).

## What IQE Does — and For Whom

IQE epitaxially grew compound-semiconductor wafer structures using MOCVD and MBE, and the company said its broader manufacturing estate also included CVD plus substrate production using Cz/LEC and VGF techniques [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). It did not design end devices or run a merchant silicon logic fab. Its role was to produce the starting material that downstream chip and photonics manufacturers then processed into finished components.

In the company’s own framing, those components served four end markets: smart connected devices, communications infrastructure, automotive and industrial, and aerospace and security [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). The GaAs portfolio addressed mobile, Wi-Fi and wireless infrastructure as well as optical communications and 3D sensing [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/). The InP portfolio addressed fibre-optic communications, hyperscale datacentres, 5G backhaul and defence systems, with IQE explicitly tying the platform to 800G AI infrastructure and cloud services [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/). The GaN franchise covered 5G base stations, radar, satellite communications, electric-vehicle power electronics and datacentre power management [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/) [Communications Infrastructure](https://www.iqep.com/markets/communications-infrastructure/).

## Leadership in Transition

The executive team changed sharply in late 2024. On 29 October 2024, IQE announced that Americo Lemos had left with immediate effect, that Mark Cubitt had moved from chair-elect to executive chair, and that CFO Jutta Meier had become interim CEO in addition to retaining finance [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/). The same release said Phil Smith would step down from the chair while remaining on the board as a non-executive director; the 2024 annual report later recorded that he remained on the board until 31 December 2024 [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/) [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf).

On 13 May 2025, the board confirmed Meier as permanent chief executive while keeping the CFO portfolio in the same pair of hands [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

> "Jutta has stabilised and refocused the business and rebuilt confidence with both customers and employees since taking the interim role." [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/)

## Revenue: The Compression Cycle

The financial trajectory through this period illustrated the cost of facility under-utilisation in a capital-intensive epitaxy business:

| Fiscal Year | Revenue (£m) | Note |
|-------------|-------------|------|
| 2019 | 140.0 | Pre-peak baseline |
| 2020 | 178.0 | VCSEL-cycle peak |
| 2021 | 154.1 | Post-peak normalisation |
| 2022 | 167.5 | Partial recovery |
| 2023 | 115.3 | Sharp compression |
| 2024 | 118.0 | Broadly flat; wireless +25%, photonics −16% |
| 2025e | c.97.0 | Trading update within frozen window |

*Sources: [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/) [Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/trading-update/)*

The 2017–2020 surge traced to the 3D-sensing VCSEL cycle. When that cycle normalised, the enlarged US footprint became a drag on margin absorption. For FY 2024, IQE reported a loss before tax of £36.9m, an adjusted loss before tax of £22.3m, adjusted EBITDA of £8.1m, and adjusted net debt of £18.8m [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). Within the year, the two principal segments diverged: wireless revenue rose to £67.3m while photonics fell to £49.9m [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

## The InP Demand Signal

Against that backdrop, the structural thesis entering 2025 centred on indium phosphide. In March 2024, IQE expanded its high-speed photonics portfolio with a 6-inch InP PIN photodetector platform and launched what it called the industry’s first foundry epitaxy service for 1310nm quantum-dot lasers on GaAs and silicon [InP portfolio expansion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-enhances-ai-connectivity-for-data-communications-with-advanced-high-speed-portfolio-expansion/). By September 2025, management was pointing to "strong performance in InP data communications for AI markets" even as other photonics end-markets remained soft [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

That InP signal crystallised commercially in April 2026, when IQE announced an £81m fundraising led by MACOM Technology Solutions. The package comprised £30m of new equity for 151,515,151 shares at 19.8p, £15m of zero-coupon convertible loan notes from MACOM, £22.8m of reinvestment by existing noteholders, an £11m placing, and a retail offer of up to £2m; the company also said MACOM was an existing customer and that long-term strategic supply agreements would accompany the investment [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/). The announcement set 15 May 2026 as the date for the shareholder vote needed to complete the package [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/).

The central tension the dossier examined was whether this convergence — InP demand pull from AI data-centre optical interconnect, a partial wireless recovery, and balance-sheet recapitalisation — would convert IQE's structurally important position in compound semiconductor epitaxy into a sustainable profit franchise, or whether the capital intensity embedded in the footprint would continue to overwhelm the cyclical recovery.

chapters.title: From 1988 Cardiff to the 2024 CEO reset
chapters.body:
## Cardiff and the original photonics business

IQE’s own heritage record anchored the company in 1988, when its first MOCVD-based manufacturing operation was established in Cardiff under the name Epitaxial Products International [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/). Between 1988 and 1998, the Cardiff business mainly served optical-communications markets, supplying photonic products used to make LEDs, lasers and photodetectors [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/).

That origin mattered because IQE did not begin life as a broad semiconductor conglomerate. It began as a specialist epitaxy house. The company’s lane was the controlled growth of compound-semiconductor wafers that other manufacturers would later turn into finished devices. That identity endured through every later expansion phase [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/) [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/).

## 1999: Bethlehem, RF and the creation of the group

The next decisive step came in 1999. IQE’s heritage page said the Cardiff MOCVD operation was complemented by the addition of an established North American facility in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, creating what the company described as the world’s leading epiwafer group with the widest range of compound-semiconductor wafer products [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/). The industrial logic was explicit: Cardiff brought optical-telecommunications depth; Bethlehem brought RF products aimed at the growing mobile-communications market [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/).

Shortly afterwards the group completed its IPO. The same heritage record said the post-IPO expansion added Wafer Technology in the UK and created IQE Silicon in Cardiff to focus on silicon-based epitaxial services [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/). By the turn of the century, the public-market company that emerged was already broader than a single-site Welsh materials specialist. It combined compound-semiconductor epitaxy, specialist substrates and a growing international footprint.

## 2006-2015: geographic scale and technology accumulation

The middle phase of the history was less theatrical but strategically important. IQE’s heritage page said two further manufacturing operations joined the group in 2006, one in the US and one in Singapore, strengthening the claim to a genuinely global manufacturing presence [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/). In 2009 the group acquired NanoGan, a University of Bath spin-out, and in 2010 it acquired Galaxy Semiconductors in Spokane, Washington, extending the infrared offering in gallium antimonide and indium antimonide and improving access to US markets [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/).

IQE accelerated that build-out in 2012. The heritage page said the group acquired the epitaxial business of Kopin and RFMD’s epitaxial division, bringing facilities in North Carolina, Massachusetts and Taiwan while consolidating market leadership [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/). In 2014 it formed the Compound Semiconductor Development Centre in Singapore through a joint venture, and in 2015 it announced a joint venture with Cardiff University to help commercialise compound-semiconductor technologies in Europe [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/).

Those steps broadened the company in three dimensions at once: geography, material systems and applications. By the middle of the 2010s IQE was no longer simply a Cardiff-and-Bethlehem enterprise. It had become a multi-site merchant epitaxy group spanning the UK, the US and Asia, with exposure to RF, photonics, infrared, power and substrates [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/) [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/).

## Newport and the 2017-2018 investment cycle

The most visible expression of that ambition was Newport. IQE’s heritage page said the company announced a new state-of-the-art mega foundry in Newport, Wales in September 2017. The first product was shipped from the facility in 2018, and the site was described as ultimately capable of housing up to 100 high-volume production tools [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/).

The same heritage record showed that 2018 was not a one-site story. IQE relocated research and development activities from Bath to Cardiff, installed additional wireless capacity in Hsinchu, expanded gallium nitride capacity in Taunton, and added gallium antimonide and indium antimonide infrared capacity in Milton Keynes [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/). The company was effectively building out for several future markets at once: 3D sensing, wireless, GaN power and infrared.

That programme later came to symbolise both the strength and weakness of IQE’s model. The strength was that management had built a real industrial footprint across multiple compound-semiconductor technologies. The weakness was that a footprint of that scale required sustained throughput to earn an adequate return.

## From diversification story to utilisation problem

The financial record made clear when that strain emerged. Summary financials showed revenue moving from £140.0m in 2019 to a peak of £178.0m in 2020, before falling to £154.1m in 2021, recovering to £167.5m in 2022 and then dropping to £115.3m in 2023 [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/). The FY2023 results statement described a market hit by high inventory levels, delays to 5G infrastructure deployment and a slowdown in Asian telecom infrastructure programmes [FY 2023 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/full-year-2023-results/).

IQE’s response was not to retreat from the compound-semiconductor thesis. It was to defend the core wireless and photonics franchises while trying to diversify further into GaN Power and microLED. The FY2023 results highlighted new customer design wins in power electronics and automotive, a new VCSEL capability for high-speed optical interconnects used in AI datacentres, and a developing 8-inch display platform [FY 2023 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/full-year-2023-results/).

## 2024-2026: rationalisation and recapitalisation

The later history inside the frozen window was therefore less about founding mythology than about balance-sheet repair. In December 2024, IQE announced completion of the sale of its decommissioned Bethlehem, Pennsylvania site and said the site’s expertise, IP, assets and customers had been transferred to Greensboro, North Carolina as part of its global consolidation strategy [Pennsylvania site sale](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-completion-of-pennsylvania-site-sale-process-as-part-of-global-consolidation-strategy/). The FY2024 results said the group had completed the consolidation of its Pennsylvania MBE operations into North Carolina, begun to consolidate South Wales operations into Newport, reduced headcount by more than 10%, and cut adjusted SG&A by 8% [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

At the same time the board and executive structure changed. Americo Lemos left on 29 October 2024; Mark Cubitt moved into the executive-chair role; Jutta Meier became interim chief executive and was then confirmed as permanent CEO on 13 May 2025 [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/) [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). The strategic review that began around the proposed Taiwan IPO later widened to include all group assets and, by April 2026, concluded with the MACOM-led £81m fundraising and associated long-term supply agreements described elsewhere in the dossier [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/) [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/).

## What the history actually showed

The cleanest way to read IQE’s history from its own records is not as a sequence of disconnected booms and busts. It is as the history of a company that kept extending a pure-play epitaxy model across new materials, new geographies and new end-markets, and then had to refinance and rationalise when demand failed to keep pace with the installed base.

By 23 May 2026 the essential historical facts were clear. The Cardiff operation founded in 1988 had grown into a global merchant epitaxy group through acquisition, site build-out and technology expansion [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/) [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). The company still described itself as the world’s only pure-play epitaxy provider with a global footprint [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). What had changed was not the industrial identity but the financial context: the same history that created strategic relevance also created the utilisation burden that dominated the later chapters of the dossier.

chapters.title: GaAs RF, InP photonics, VCSEL, GaN, and the AI-driven InP inflection
chapters.body:
## Reporting segments and product platforms

By the frozen window, IQE described itself through two overlapping lenses. Public financial reporting still broke the business into Wireless, Photonics and the residual CMOS++ line, while the product and market pages described the technical portfolio through material systems such as gallium arsenide, indium phosphide, gallium nitride, gallium antimonide and specialist substrates [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/) [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/) [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/).

The economic mix in the official accounts remained heavily concentrated in two segments:

| Period | Wireless revenue | Photonics revenue | CMOS++ revenue |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY 2023 | £53.9m | £59.1m | £2.3m |
| FY 2024 | £67.3m | £49.9m | £0.8m |
| H1 2025 | £18.6m | £26.6m | not separately reported |

*Sources: [FY 2023 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/full-year-2023-results/) [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/) [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/)*

The FY2024 results also said that from FY2025 onward IQE would no longer report CMOS++ as a standalone segment, which was itself a signal that the line had become strategically subordinate to the wider diversification effort into GaN Power and microLED [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

## Wireless: the GaAs revenue engine

Wireless remained the core commercial franchise through the period. IQE’s GaAs page said gallium arsenide epitaxy had been central to the group’s leadership since 1988 and that the portfolio served mobile, Wi-Fi and wireless infrastructure, alongside optical communications, sensing and display applications [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/). The page listed pHEMT, MESFET and HFET structures, GaAs PIN and Schottky diodes, InGaP/GaAs and AlGaAs/GaAs HBT families, and VCSEL structures at 850nm, 940nm and 1060nm [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/).

The reported financial mix supported that centrality. In FY2024, wireless revenue rose 24.9% to £67.295m from £53.877m, which the company attributed to higher penetration in Asian markets for wireless GaAs and higher GaN sales for 5G infrastructure [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). The same documents made clear, however, that this was a recovery within a cyclical business rather than a straight line upward. In H1 2025, wireless revenue fell to £18.6m from £38.8m a year earlier as customer inventory overhang, tariff uncertainty and softness in mobile-handset demand weighed on orders [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

The right reading was therefore that GaAs remained the group’s revenue engine, but not an uncomplicated growth engine. It provided the largest installed base of business and the quickest route to volume when inventory normalised, yet it also left IQE tied to handset, Wi-Fi and infrastructure cycles that could reverse abruptly.

## Photonics: from sensing exposure to InP and AI datacom

Photonics was the second major segment, but it was not one business. The official record showed at least three overlapping product families inside it: legacy and current VCSEL structures, indium phosphide datacom and telecom devices, and infrared materials aimed at aerospace and security applications [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/).

The InP page was particularly revealing about where management wanted the narrative to move. IQE said indium phosphide underpinned global fibre-optic communications and was a platform for next-generation AI and terahertz communications, enabling modern AI infrastructure and cloud services up to 800G [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/). The same page listed FP, DFB and EML laser structures, APDs and photodetectors, quantum cascade lasers, SWIR photodetectors, and InP HBTs and HEMTs [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/). The AI and Datacentres page then explicitly tied InP and GaAs wafers to the lasers, photodiodes and modulators used in high-speed optical links for cloud and hyperscale networks [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/).

The financial pattern showed the transition in progress rather than completed. FY2024 photonics revenue fell 15.6% to £49.876m as weakness in 3D sensing and telecoms infrastructure outweighed stronger aerospace and security demand [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). Yet the company’s development milestones increasingly pointed toward AI-linked datacom. In H1 2024, IQE said it had qualified InP laser technology for high-speed optical transceivers deployed within large-scale generative-AI datacentres and had qualified quantum-dot-laser products with an industry-leading silicon-photonics customer [2024 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/2024-interim-results/). In FY2024, the annual report said the group qualified quantum-dot-laser products for an industry-leading silicon-photonics customer and deepened its partnership with Quintessent to establish what it called the world’s first large-scale QDL supply chain [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf).

By H1 2025, photonics revenue was broadly flat at £26.6m despite broader weakness, which management said reflected strong InP data-communications performance for AI markets partly offset by delays in US military and defence infrared funding [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/). That was the clearest evidence inside the frozen window that the photonics mix was rotating.

## VCSELs: still present, but no longer the organising principle

The product pages showed that VCSEL structures remained embedded inside IQE’s GaAs franchise. The company continued to offer multi-junction VCSELs for 3D sensing and cited applications in optical communications, facial-recognition systems and AR/VR displays [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/). Official updates during 2024 and 2025 reinforced that continuity. H1 2024 disclosures referenced delivery of next-generation 3D-sensing VCSEL products for module-level qualification in new AR/VR and mobile platforms, while the annual report said IQE had delivered higher-performance VCSEL products for qualification in new mobile platforms including AR/VR [2024 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/2024-interim-results/) [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf).

But the same official record also showed that VCSEL was no longer the single organising principle of the equity story. Management’s language increasingly prioritised InP datacom, GaN Power and microLED diversification. VCSEL remained commercially relevant; it was no longer the only growth narrative carrying the dossier.

## GaN Power and infrastructure: the diversification lane

GaN was the clearest official diversification theme. IQE’s GaN page described the platform as a wide-bandgap semiconductor spanning RF, power, photonics and display markets, with products across SiC, Si, GaN, sapphire and engineered substrates [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/). The page listed GaN RF HEMTs on SiC and Si, 650V depletion-mode and enhancement-mode devices, vertical GaN-on-GaN structures for high-voltage power, GaN-on-sapphire for power electronics, and RGB GaN-on-silicon microLEDs [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/).

The official reporting trail showed that this was more than a brochure claim. FY2023 results said IQE was deploying GaN Power capacity in the US and UK, building a customer pipeline across fabless companies, foundries and OEMs serving automotive and emerging datacentre-server power markets [FY 2023 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/full-year-2023-results/). FY2024 results said the group had received its first commercial orders for 650V automotive qualifications and had tools qualified to serve forthcoming GaN opportunities [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). H1 2025 then added a progressing joint development agreement with X-FAB, sampling with leading automotive power customers, and work on higher-voltage GaN above 1000V through government-funded programmes [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

That progression mattered strategically because it broadened the company beyond handset RF and photonics. It also mattered financially because GaN Power was one of the diversification lanes through which management hoped to fill under-used assets without needing a fresh greenfield build.

## Display, infrared and the substrate base

The smaller technical franchises were not irrelevant. IQE’s 2024 and 2025 disclosures highlighted an 8-inch GaAs and GaN RGB microLED product portfolio, continued engagement with Tier 1 consumer-mobile and display manufacturers, and an ongoing partnership with a leading smart-glasses developer [2024 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/2024-interim-results/) [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). H1 2025 added a customer partnership aimed at microLEDs for high-density, power-efficient datacom interconnects and continued development work in new display ecosystems [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

Infrared and substrates also remained part of the real business rather than historical leftovers. The global-footprint and product pages listed GaSb, InSb, InAs, InP and GaAs substrate lines [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). H1 2025 results said IQE had delivered its first commercial orders for 6-inch GaSb epiwafers for large-area imaging products aimed at space and satellite applications [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

## What the segment mix implied

The segment and product record showed a business with two present-tense cash engines and several option-like programmes around them. Wireless and photonics still determined the income statement. GaN Power, display and specialist infrared products were the development lanes that management hoped would reduce dependence on any one cycle [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/) [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

That also explained why the dossier could not be read as a simple “five equal platforms” story. The technical breadth was real, but the economic concentration was real as well. IQE had a wide menu of materials and applications; it still needed the largest of them to carry the fixed-cost base while the newer franchises matured.

chapters.title: GBP 115M revenue, the capacity utilisation problem, and the InP-driven recovery path
chapters.body:
## The income statement in three years

The official accounts showed a business that did not collapse in 2024 so much as fail to recover enough. The easiest way to see that was to place the last three full years side by side:

| Metric | FY 2022 | FY 2023 | FY 2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | £167.5m | £115.3m | £118.0m |
| Adjusted EBITDA | £23.4m | £4.3m | £8.1m |
| Adjusted operating profit/(loss) | £(3.6)m | £(20.2)m | £(18.4)m |
| Reported operating profit/(loss) | £(73.0)m | £(25.8)m | £(33.0)m |
| Reported net cashflow from operations | £8.9m | £10.1m | £1.3m |
| Cash capital expenditure | £9.4m | £12.2m | £11.4m |
| Adjusted net debt | £15.2m | £2.2m | £18.8m |
| Cash and cash equivalents | £11.6m | £5.6m | £4.7m |

*Sources: [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/) [FY 2023 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/full-year-2023-results/) [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/)*

The shift that mattered most was not the 2024 revenue increase of 2.4% in isolation. It was the fact that a move from £115.3m to £118.0m still left the group deeply subscale against its fixed manufacturing base [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). Adjusted EBITDA improved from £4.3m to £8.1m, but adjusted operating loss remained £18.4m and cash generation weakened sharply [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/) [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

## Why 2024 still looked weak despite “improvement”

The FY2024 results did contain genuine progress. Wireless revenue rose 24.9% to £67.3m as Asian-market penetration improved and GaN sales for 5G infrastructure increased [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 7% from 4% in 2023, which management attributed to prior-year cost mitigation, further cost management in 2024, and manufacturing-site consolidation [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

But the same disclosure also explained why the overall result remained poor. Photonics revenue fell 16% to £49.9m because of softness in 3D sensing and telecoms infrastructure, partly offset by infrared strength in aerospace and security [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). CMOS++ revenue dropped to £0.8m and was effectively being phased out as a separately reported line [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). Reported operating loss widened to £33.0m because the year carried £7.6m of restructuring costs and £3.1m of non-cash asset impairments related to the US wireless business, alongside further non-cash impairment charges tied to manufacturing consolidation [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

The annual report put the gross-profit point plainly. Statutory gross profit rose only to £4.446m from £2.328m despite the revenue increase, reflecting how little room there still was between throughput and fixed cost [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). This was not a broken accounting story. It was a utilisation story.

## The half-year pattern showed the volatility

The interim statements made that same point in compressed form. H1 2024 looked like a stabilisation phase: revenue was £66.0m, adjusted EBITDA was £6.6m, wireless revenue rose 73% year on year to £38.8m, and labour costs were reduced by roughly 10% year on year while non-labour costs fell around 5% [2024 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/2024-interim-results/). Management also said sale of the decommissioned Pennsylvania site was expected in H2 2024 [2024 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/2024-interim-results/).

H1 2025 then showed how fragile that improvement had been. Revenue fell to £45.3m from £66.0m, wireless revenue halved to £18.6m, and adjusted EBITDA swung to a £0.4m loss [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/). Management attributed the wireless drop to 2024 customer inventory overhang, tariff uncertainty and soft consumer mobile demand, while photonics held broadly flat at £26.6m because strong InP data-communications performance for AI markets offset delays in US military and defence infrared programmes [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

The interim record therefore reinforced the central reading of the full-year numbers. IQE did not have a broad enough revenue base to smooth out programme and inventory shocks. Improvement in one lane could be overwhelmed by weakness in another because the cost base kept accruing regardless.

## Cash, capex and the footprint burden

Capital spending did come down, but only gradually. FY2023 cash capital expenditure was £12.2m and FY2024 was still £11.4m [FY 2023 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/full-year-2023-results/) [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). H1 2025 was the first reporting period that showed a more aggressive pullback, with cash capital expenditure of only £1.0m [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/). That was the financial signature of a company preserving liquidity while still trying to fund selected diversification programmes.

Management paired that capex discipline with asset rationalisation. In December 2024, IQE announced completion of the sale of the decommissioned Pennsylvania site for $5.5m and said the site’s expertise, IP, assets and customers had already been transferred to Greensboro, North Carolina [Pennsylvania site sale](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-completion-of-pennsylvania-site-sale-process-as-part-of-global-consolidation-strategy/). The FY2024 results added that Pennsylvania MBE operations had been fully consolidated into North Carolina and that South Wales operations were beginning to consolidate into Newport [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

Those moves improved the shape of the estate but did not eliminate the burden of it. Even after cost actions, the annual report said the group had 479 employees at 31 December 2024 and maintained a footprint across the UK, the US and Taiwan [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf) [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/).

## The financing bridge

Liquidity pressure forced a two-step refinancing. On 24 January 2025, IQE announced an £18m zero-coupon convertible loan note financing led by Lombard Odier, with a 12-month maturity, a six-month extension option and a 15p conversion price [Convertible Loan Note Financing](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/convertible-loan-note-financing/). On 14 March 2025, it confirmed that the financing had closed [Closing of CLN Financing](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/closing-of-convertible-loan-note-financing/).

That deal bought time. It did not solve the underlying economic problem. By September 2025, management had cut FY2025 guidance to £90m-£100m and widened the strategic review from Taiwan to the whole group [Trading Update and Strategic Review Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/trading-update-and-strategic-review-update/). The January 2026 trading update then said FY2025 revenue should land at the upper end of that range, around £97m, with photonics demand stronger than previously forecast because of AI and datacentre markets [Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/trading-update/).

The longer-term fix only appeared in April 2026, when the strategic review ended with the MACOM-led £81m package described in the Snapshot chapter [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/). By then the balance-sheet question had changed from “can the group fund the next year?” to “can the group use the extra time to generate durable operating leverage?”

## What the finance chapter really said

The most important conclusion from the primary record was that IQE’s problem was not a lack of technological relevance. It was the mismatch between a strategically valuable asset base and a revenue line that remained too volatile and too low to cover it comfortably.

Official numbers showed the sequence clearly. FY2023 was the trough year on revenue and profitability [FY 2023 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/full-year-2023-results/). FY2024 brought partial operational improvement but not enough cash conversion [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). H1 2025 showed that wireless destocking could still undo the prior year’s progress [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/). The recapitalisations of March 2025 and April 2026 addressed liquidity. What they did not yet prove, by 23 May 2026, was that the group had crossed back to a sustainable earnings model.

chapters.title: From the 2020 VCSEL peak to the 2024 reset and the InP inflection
chapters.body:
## The VCSEL zenith: fiscal year 2020

The £178.0m of revenue that IQE recorded in 2020 marked the high-water mark of the VCSEL cycle [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/). In retrospect, that peak concealed the vulnerability of a fixed-cost manufacturing estate built for a demand curve that did not continue at the same pitch.

## Normalisation and the false dawn: 2021–2022

Fiscal 2021 delivered the first sharp correction, with revenue falling to £154.1m [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/). Fiscal 2022 then looked, on the surface, like a recovery: revenue rebounded to £167.5m and adjusted EBITDA reached £23.4m [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/). But the more consequential development was governance rather than optics. IQE had announced Americo Lemos as CEO in November 2021, with a 10 January 2022 start date, after a board-led search; he arrived from GlobalFoundries, where he had been Senior Vice President of Business Development for Asia Pacific and China Country President [Americo Lemos appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2021/leadership-announcement-americo-lemos-appointed-as-ceo-of-iqe/).

## The trough: 2023 and the £115 million reckoning

If 2022 offered false optimism, 2023 delivered the reckoning. Full-year revenue fell to £115.3m and adjusted EBITDA collapsed to £4.3m [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/). The message from management through the period was that the asset base had been built for markets — AI-linked photonics, power electronics and next-generation wireless — that were still arriving, just more slowly than investors had expected. The numbers showed the cost of that mismatch.

## October 2024: Lemos departs, the board resets

In October 2024, after less than three years in post, Lemos left with immediate effect [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/). The same release moved Mark Cubitt into the executive chair role and elevated Jutta Meier — who had joined only in January 2024 as CFO — to interim CEO while keeping the finance brief [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/). Phil Smith stepped down from the chair at that point and remained on the board as a non-executive director until the end of the year [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/) [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf).

The board did not repudiate the strategic direction. It instead reframed the immediate problem as one of pace, liquidity and asset optimisation. The 23 January 2025 pre-close update said FY24 revenue and adjusted EBITDA would exceed prior expectations and linked that improvement directly to cost control and operational performance [Pre-close Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/pre-close-trading-update/).

## 2025 and the InP inflection thesis

Meier’s permanent appointment on 13 May 2025 formalised the interim arrangement [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). By then, the company was explicitly framing the next recovery leg around AI-related photonics: the InP product platform, optical communications, aerospace and security, and further diversification in GaN power [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/) [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/).

## Equity positioning and the test ahead

The clearest market marker of how far the equity story had reset came in the April 2026 MACOM-led fundraising. IQE priced the issue at 19.8p, which it said represented a 58.4% discount to the 24 April 2026 closing mid-market price of 47.6p [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/). That was not the language of a company raising growth equity from a position of strength. It was the pricing of a business recapitalising after a prolonged utilisation shock.

By the snapshot date, the analytical question had narrowed. The company no longer needed to prove that InP mattered to AI-linked optical infrastructure; its own product and market disclosures already made that case [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/). It needed to prove that enough of that demand would convert into shipments, gross-margin recovery and cash generation before the next financing discussion reopened.

chapters.title: Steve Smith (CEO), Jutta Meier, and the Non-Executive Chair
chapters.body:
Despite the draft chapter title, the primary record showed no executive named Steve Smith at IQE. The succession that mattered through the frozen window was from Americo Lemos to Jutta Meier, with Mark Cubitt moving from chair-elect to executive chair and then remaining board chair through the 2026 recapitalisation [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/) [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/).

## The Lemos Era: January 2022 – October 2024

IQE announced Lemos’s appointment on 22 November 2021, with a 10 January 2022 start date [Americo Lemos appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2021/leadership-announcement-americo-lemos-appointed-as-ceo-of-iqe/). The company said he was joining from GlobalFoundries, where he had been Senior Vice President of Business Development for Asia Pacific and China Country President, after earlier roles at Qualcomm, Intel, Flextronics, Texas Instruments and Skyworks [Americo Lemos appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2021/leadership-announcement-americo-lemos-appointed-as-ceo-of-iqe/). His joining award was a £200,000 share issuance subject to a three-year clawback [Americo Lemos appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2021/leadership-announcement-americo-lemos-appointed-as-ceo-of-iqe/).

Lemos inherited a business already exposed to the post-VCSEL reset. Over the period that followed, revenue moved from £167.5m in 2022 to £115.3m in 2023, while adjusted EBITDA fell from £23.4m to £4.3m [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/). When IQE announced his departure on 29 October 2024, the board did not offer a narrative explanation. What it did say was that the immediate priorities for Cubitt and Meier would be executing the near-term pipeline, generating cash across the group, pursuing the Taiwan IPO and examining further asset optimisation [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/).

## Jutta Meier: From Intel Foundry to Chief Executive

IQE appointed Jutta Meier as CFO on 16 January 2024, effective 22 January [Jutta Meier CFO appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/appointment-of-jutta-meier-as-chief-financial-officer/). The announcement said she had spent more than 25 years in senior semiconductor finance roles, most recently as Senior Finance Director at Intel Foundry Services and earlier as Vice President of Finance at GlobalFoundries and in a range of roles at AMD [Jutta Meier CFO appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/appointment-of-jutta-meier-as-chief-financial-officer/). At appointment she was 57 and received a £200,000 new-starter options award vesting in two equal tranches over two years [Jutta Meier CFO appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/appointment-of-jutta-meier-as-chief-financial-officer/).

Nine months later, Meier was interim CEO as well as CFO [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/). On 13 May 2025 the board confirmed her as permanent chief executive while keeping the CFO remit in place [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). The same results statement showed the basis on which the board made that call: revenue of £118.0m, adjusted EBITDA of £8.1m, a headcount reduction of more than 10%, adjusted SG&A down 8%, completion of the Pennsylvania MBE consolidation into North Carolina, and a strategic review that had broadened from a Taiwan IPO to include a full sale of that subsidiary [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

## Mark Cubitt: From Chair-elect to Executive Chair

Cubitt joined the board on 8 October 2024 as an independent non-executive director and chair-elect [Mark Cubitt appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/appointment-of-non-executive-director-and-chair-elect/). IQE said at the time that he was expected to succeed Phil Smith as chair in H1 2025 after a transition period, and highlighted both his concurrent chairmanships at Concurrent Technologies and Beeks Financial Cloud Group and his more than seven years as CFO of Wolfson Microelectronics [Mark Cubitt appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/appointment-of-non-executive-director-and-chair-elect/). The Lemos departure accelerated that timetable: by 29 October, Cubitt was executive chair [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/).

He remained central to the story thereafter. The March 2025 closing of the convertible loan note financing identified him as executive chair and disclosed that he had personally participated in the £18m financing [Closing of CLN Financing](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/closing-of-convertible-loan-note-financing/). The April 2026 MACOM announcement referred to him as chair and carried his statement that the strategic review had produced "a fantastic outcome for all stakeholders" [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/).

## The Non-Executive Bench

The 2024 annual report showed a non-executive bench with deep semiconductor and capital-markets overlap. Carol Chesney served as senior independent director and audit chair; the report said she also held external audit-chair or board roles at Hunting, Hill & Smith and Imagination Technologies, having previously served at Renishaw and Biffa [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). Victoria Hull, who had joined IQE in August 2021, was described there as senior independent director and nominations chair at Hikma Pharmaceuticals and remuneration chair at IMI and Serco [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). Maria Marced and Bami Bastani joined from 1 January 2024, bringing long operating histories from TSMC Europe, Intel, NXP and GlobalFoundries [IQE Board appointments](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2023/iqe-board-appointments/). Harmesh Suniara, the Lombard Odier representative, gave the company’s largest shareholder a direct board seat through the restructuring and financing cycle [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf) [Convertible Loan Note Financing](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/convertible-loan-note-financing/).

## Governance Architecture

What mattered by the frozen window was not cosmetic governance hygiene but operational control. IQE’s board had concentrated executive authority in a Meier-Cubitt pairing while it reworked the footprint, ran the Taiwan strategic process, raised the £18m convertible loan note, widened the review to include a possible sale of the whole company, and then concluded the process with the £81m MACOM package [Pre-close Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/pre-close-trading-update/) [Trading Update and Strategic Review Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/trading-update-and-strategic-review-update/) [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/). IQE also said female representation on the board stood at 57% after Meier’s promotion [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

No public announcement within the frozen window set out a timetable for separating the CEO and CFO portfolios again. Through 23 May 2026, the structure remained exactly what the board had formalised in May 2025: Jutta Meier as CEO and CFO, supported by Mark Cubitt as chair.

chapters.title: Qorvo, Lumentum, Coherent, and the foundry-and-substrate supply chain
chapters.body:
## A Merchant Foundry at the Centre of the Stack

IQE plc sat at a specific position in the compound semiconductor value chain: it grew the epitaxial layers on which downstream device makers then fabricated their circuits. That positioning gave the company unusual breadth, but it also meant the revenue line was mediated by a relatively small number of large wireless, photonics and industrial programmes rather than by diversified mass-market end demand [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

The company itself framed that revenue base through segments and end markets rather than by naming most customers. Wireless remained the larger segment in 2024, accounting for £67.3m of sales, while photonics contributed £49.9m and CMOS++ just £0.8m [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). Across those segments, IQE said it served smart connected devices, communications infrastructure, automotive and industrial, and aerospace and security [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

## The RF Customer Base: GaAs and the 5G Amplifier Supply Chain

The GaAs RF line remained the company’s commercial engine. IQE’s GaAs product page described the platform as central to mobile, Wi-Fi and wireless infrastructure, while also covering optical communications, 3D sensing and red microLEDs [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/). In 2024, wireless revenue rose 25% year on year as Asian-market penetration improved and GaN demand for 5G infrastructure strengthened [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

That did not mean the wireless book had become stable. The September 2025 trading update said weakness in mobile handset sales was still depressing the segment and that some end demand was being fulfilled from existing inventory rather than fresh orders [Trading Update and Strategic Review Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/trading-update-and-strategic-review-update/). IQE’s wireless customer architecture therefore looked less like a smooth secular curve than a set of highly qualified programmes exposed to inventory swings at handset and infrastructure OEM level.

## Photonics, VCSEL and the InP Datacentre Shift

The photonics story divided into two phases. The first was the 3D-sensing/VCSEL cycle, which carried IQE to its 2020 revenue peak and then unwound. The second was the move toward optical interconnect, AI-linked datacentre demand and defence-related sensing. On its product and market pages, IQE said InP and GaAs wafers enabled lasers, photodiodes and modulators for high-speed optical links in cloud and hyperscale networks, while GaN supported datacentre power efficiency [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/).

The financial record showed the crossover still in progress. Photonics revenue fell 15.6% in 2024 to £49.876m as softness in 3D sensing and telecom infrastructure outweighed the better performance of infrared products in aerospace and security [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). By January 2026, however, IQE said photonics demand had come in higher than forecast in H2 2025, reflecting continued growth in AI and datacentre markets [Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/trading-update/).

## Foundry Partners and Broader Programme Architecture

Not all of IQE’s demand sat in a simple merchant-to-device-maker chain. Some of it ran through foundry relationships, joint-development agreements and geographically specific manufacturing programmes. The clearest disclosed example in the frozen window was the company’s joint development agreement with X-FAB to create a Europe-based GaN power device platform for automotive, datacentre and consumer applications [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). That kind of partnership reinforced the point that IQE’s supply chain role was often embedded in a broader process stack rather than sold as a commodity wafer into an open market.

The manufacturing footprint supported that model. IQE’s sites page listed Cardiff, Newport, Milton Keynes, Taunton, Greensboro, Spokane and Taiwan as active locations within the group’s operating network by the snapshot period [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). That mattered commercially because it offered both technical breadth and geographic redundancy.

## Upstream: Substrates, Chemicals and Equipment

IQE’s own supply chain remained specialised. The global-footprint page said the group manufactured using MOCVD, MBE and CVD technologies and also ran substrate production using Cz/LEC and VGF techniques [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). The product portfolio made clear that each material system carried distinct technical dependencies: GaAs covered HBTs, pHEMTs and VCSEL structures; InP covered FP, DFB and EML lasers, APDs and photodetectors; GaN covered RF HEMTs and high-voltage power structures across multiple substrate types [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/).

## Geographic Exposure and Trade Policy

The earlier draft understated what IQE actually disclosed about China exposure. The 2024 annual report broke revenue out geographically and showed Asia-Pacific revenue of £41.095m, of which £27.142m came from Taiwan, £6.456m from Japan and £1.928m from the People’s Republic of China [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). The US contributed £51.974m and the UK £12.642m [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). The right conclusion, therefore, was not that IQE had disclosed no direct China revenue, but that direct PRC exposure was modest beside Taiwan and US demand and that the larger risk sat in the wider Asian electronics and handset supply chain.

chapters.title: Where IQE sits in compound semiconductor epitaxy
chapters.body:
## The merchant model in a fragmented industry

Compound semiconductor epitaxy is not organised like the mainstream silicon industry. The market sits across three overlapping supply modes: independent merchant growers, vertically integrated device manufacturers that keep epitaxy in-house, and foundry-integrated specialty-process platforms. IQE’s own language captured where it believed it stood inside that map: the company called itself the world’s only pure-play epitaxy provider with a global footprint and described itself elsewhere as the scaled global epitaxy leader [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/) [Americo Lemos appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2021/leadership-announcement-americo-lemos-appointed-as-ceo-of-iqe/).

The merchant model existed because compound semiconductor growth remained difficult to internalise at subscale. IQE’s portfolio spanned GaAs, InP, GaN, GaSb, SiGe and multiple substrate lines, each with its own reactor chemistry, process control and qualification burden [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/) [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). That breadth made the company unusual even before any discussion of market share.

## IQE's breadth among independent suppliers

What could be verified directly from company materials was not a precise league table, but breadth. The active footprint at the snapshot date covered Cardiff, Newport, Milton Keynes, Taunton, Greensboro, Spokane and Taiwan, with manufacturing across MOCVD, MBE and CVD and substrate production using Cz/LEC and VGF [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). The product set ranged from GaAs RF and VCSEL structures to InP optical components, GaN RF and power devices, GaSb infrared materials and specialised substrates [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/).

That breadth mattered strategically because it let IQE present itself not as a single-material house but as a cross-platform merchant supplier. The company’s 2024 results explicitly linked that positioning to growth ambitions in AI/datacentre optical communications, aerospace and security, GaN power, microLED displays and next-generation wireless [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/).

## Captive epi at integrated device makers

The most durable competitive pressure on the merchant model came from integrated manufacturers that could absorb epitaxy inside a broader device margin. IQE itself did not provide a public counterparty-by-counterparty map of those competitors in the cited filings. What it did show, however, was that the addressable market for a merchant grower was always conditional: a programme won by an integrated device maker with in-house growth capability might never appear in the merchant wafer market at all.

That point mattered most in photonics. IQE’s AI and datacentre materials positioned InP, GaAs and GaN squarely inside optical interconnect, high-speed links and power-efficiency upgrades [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/). If those growth vectors scaled primarily through customers that continued to buy merchant epitaxy, IQE’s utilisation upside was substantial. If they scaled through customers that internalised a larger share of the growth step, the secular end-market tailwind would not translate one-for-one into IQE revenue.

## Foundry-integrated compound semiconductor flows

A third competitive mode sat between pure merchant supply and full vertical integration: foundry-integrated specialty-process platforms. IQE’s own disclosures showed that this was not merely a theoretical category. The company had active development relationships with foundry and platform partners, including the X-FAB joint development agreement in GaN power announced with the FY 2024 results [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). Those arrangements created opportunity, but they also illustrated the structural reality that some epitaxy value could be captured inside a broader foundry ecosystem rather than sold as a standalone merchant wafer.

## The InP arena and the AI photonics inflection

The sharpest competitive question by the snapshot date sat in InP. IQE’s market and product pages described InP as central to global fibre networks, hyperscale datacentres, 800G AI infrastructure, cloud services, 5G backhaul and secure defence systems [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/). The company’s January 2026 trading update then said photonics demand had come in above forecast because of continued growth in AI and datacentre markets [Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/trading-update/).

The contest, therefore, was not whether AI optical interconnect mattered. It was whether merchant epitaxy retained enough of that value pool. IQE’s argument rested on scale, qualification depth, product breadth and footprint redundancy. The counter-argument was that the most attractive end-markets were precisely those that might justify more in-house or platform-integrated control by large device makers.

| Supply model | Core feature | IQE implication |
|---|---|---|
| Merchant epitaxy | Independent wafer growth sold into multiple end markets | Favourable to IQE’s breadth and multi-site footprint |
| Captive IDM growth | Epitaxy kept inside an integrated device margin | Reduces merchant addressable volume |
| Foundry-integrated specialty flow | Epitaxy bundled inside a larger process platform | Creates partnership routes but compresses standalone merchant share |

IQE’s strategic case remained coherent: a single supplier with meaningful capability across GaAs, InP, GaN and related materials could still offer second-source insurance, qualification leverage and cross-platform procurement simplicity. Whether that was enough to capture disproportionate share in the AI photonics cycle remained one of the central open questions as the frozen window closed.

chapters.title: From the 2018 Bethlehem opening to the 2024 CEO reset and the InP inflection
chapters.body:
## The Bethlehem Bet

IQE’s capital story still traced back to the expansion years. The heritage page recorded that the company’s Newport mega-foundry shipped first product in 2018, while the broader US and Taiwan expansion programme added wireless capacity in Hsinchu and more GaN capacity in Taunton [Heritage](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/heritage/). Those investments were the physical precondition for the company’s later argument that it could serve both sensing and AI-linked photonics without a fresh greenfield build.

## The VCSEL Cycle and Its Unwind

The revenue tape captured the cycle cleanly: £178.0m in 2020, £154.1m in 2021, £167.5m in 2022, £115.3m in 2023 and £118.0m in 2024 [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/). That was the move from VCSEL-era peak to prolonged under-utilisation. By December 2024, IQE had sold the decommissioned Bethlehem site for $5.5m and said it had transferred the site’s expertise, IP, assets and customers to Greensboro, North Carolina [Pennsylvania site sale](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-completion-of-pennsylvania-site-sale-process-as-part-of-global-consolidation-strategy/).

## Lemos and the Restructuring Imperative

Lemos’s appointment in late 2021 was framed as the arrival of a senior operator from GlobalFoundries to lead the next phase of growth [Americo Lemos appointment](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2021/leadership-announcement-americo-lemos-appointed-as-ceo-of-iqe/). By the time he left in October 2024, the company had not repaired the revenue line enough to escape a liquidity debate [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/).

## October 2024: The Board Acts

The earlier draft misidentified the protagonists. It was not Chris Meadows but Mark Cubitt who took executive control when Lemos departed, while Jutta Meier became interim CEO alongside the CFO role [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/). The release also made clear what the new leadership team had been asked to do immediately: execute the near-term pipeline, generate cash, pursue the Taiwan IPO and examine further ways to optimise the asset base [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/).

## The InP Inflection

Meier’s permanent appointment in May 2025 formalised the transition [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). By then, the company was explicitly highlighting optical communications, AI/datacentre photonics, GaN power, infrared sensing and microLED as the routes out of the trough [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/) [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/).

## Primary-source catalyst tape

The primary-source record was richer than the earlier draft suggested. On 23 January 2025, IQE said FY24 revenue would come in at £118m and adjusted EBITDA at at least £7.5m, ahead of prior expectations, while the strategic review was still focused on Taiwan and the convertible loan note was in final stages [Pre-close Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/pre-close-trading-update/). On 24 January, the company announced the terms of the £18m zero-coupon convertible loan note financing led by Lombard Odier [Convertible Loan Note Financing](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/convertible-loan-note-financing/). On 14 March, it confirmed closing of that financing [Closing of CLN Financing](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/closing-of-convertible-loan-note-financing/). On 8 September, it cut FY25 guidance to £90m-£100m and expanded the strategic review to include a possible sale of the whole company [Trading Update and Strategic Review Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/trading-update-and-strategic-review-update/). On 12 January 2026, it said FY25 should land at the upper end of that range, around £97m, helped by stronger photonics demand tied to AI and datacentres [Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/trading-update/). And on 27 April 2026, it concluded the review with the £81m MACOM-led package and long-term supply agreements [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/).

## What investors were watching by the snapshot date

By 23 May 2026, the market was no longer waiting for a new qualitative story. It was waiting to see whether footprint rationalisation, AI/datacentre photonics demand and the MACOM recapitalisation would begin to show up in utilisation, gross margin and cash generation in subsequent reporting [Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/trading-update/) [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/).

chapters.title: Epitaxy science, reactor IP, material-system breadth
chapters.body:
## Process capability, not a single product

IQE’s official materials described a company whose technical value sat in process breadth rather than in any one device design. The global-footprint page said the group manufactured using MOCVD, CVD and MBE technologies and also produced substrate materials using Cz/LEC and VGF techniques [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). That meant the technical estate spanned both epitaxial growth and parts of the specialist substrate stack, with capability distributed across sites in the UK, the US and Taiwan [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/).

The practical significance of that breadth was that IQE was not selling a single “compound semiconductor wafer” in the abstract. It was maintaining separate recipe families across GaAs, InP, GaN, GaSb and substrate lines, each with different structures, customers and qualification paths [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/) [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/).

## GaAs: the mature volume platform

IQE’s GaAs page said gallium arsenide epitaxy had been central to the company’s leadership since 1988 and that the platform was scalable to 200 mm, including on germanium substrates [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/). The official applications list covered mobile, Wi-Fi and wireless infrastructure, VCSELs and photodetectors for optical communications, multi-junction VCSELs for 3D sensing, and red emitters for display applications [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/).

The menu of structures was correspondingly broad: pHEMTs, MESFETs, HFETs, PIN and Schottky diodes, InGaP/GaAs and AlGaAs/GaAs HBT families, VCSELs at 850nm, 940nm and 1060nm, quantum-well photodetectors, and red LD/LED platforms [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/). Official updates in 2024 and 2025 showed that the GaAs franchise was still evolving rather than merely harvesting legacy demand. H1 2024 referenced delivery of high-speed data-communications VCSEL products for short-reach optical-transceiver applications and next-generation 3D-sensing VCSELs for AR/VR and mobile platforms [2024 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/2024-interim-results/). The FY2024 annual report added higher-performance VCSEL products for qualification in new mobile platforms and ongoing engagement in red microLED materials [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf).

## InP: the AI and optical-interconnect programme

The InP platform was where the technical roadmap most clearly intersected with the later investment case. IQE’s InP page said the material underpinned global fibre-optic communication networks and next-generation AI and terahertz communications, enabling cloud services and AI infrastructure up to 800G [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/). The page listed FP, DFB and EML laser structures, APDs and photodetectors, SWIR and extended-wavelength photodetectors, quantum cascade lasers, and InP HBT and HEMT structures [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/).

The research-fill gap in the original draft was that the public record did, in fact, provide specific qualification milestones. In March 2024, IQE announced a 6-inch InP PIN photodetector platform and what it called the industry’s first foundry epitaxy service for 1310nm quantum-dot lasers on GaAs and silicon [InP portfolio expansion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-enhances-ai-connectivity-for-data-communications-with-advanced-high-speed-portfolio-expansion/). In H1 2024, the group said it had qualified InP laser technology for high-speed optical transceivers deployed within large-scale generative-AI datacentres and qualified quantum-dot-laser products with an industry-leading silicon-photonics customer [2024 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/2024-interim-results/). The FY2024 annual report then said IQE had strengthened its partnership with Quintessent to establish the world’s first large-scale QDL supply chain [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf).

By H1 2025, management was explicitly reporting “strong performance in InP data communications for AI markets” within the photonics segment [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/). The technical programme had therefore moved beyond generic aspiration. It had progressed into customer qualification, supply-chain partnership and early commercial contribution.

## GaN: from RF heritage to power and display

IQE’s GaN page described gallium nitride as a wide-bandgap platform spanning RF, power, photonics and display markets, with more than 20 years of GaN innovation and product coverage across SiC, Si, GaN, sapphire and engineered substrates [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/). The official structure list included RF HEMTs on SiC and Si, 650V depletion-mode and enhancement-mode devices, vertical GaN-on-GaN for high-voltage power applications, GaN-on-sapphire for high-voltage power electronics, and RGB GaN-on-silicon microLEDs [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/).

The reporting trail again showed concrete milestones. H1 2024 said IQE had increased GaN capacity, progressed qualification of 650V depletion-mode and enhancement-mode products for Tier 1 OEMs, and continued deploying GaN Power capacity in the US and UK [2024 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/2024-interim-results/). The FY2024 annual report said the company saw successful customer demonstration of 650V products and received its first commercial orders for 650V automotive qualifications [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). H1 2025 added sampling under the X-FAB joint development agreement, work on sovereign supply chains in both the US and Europe, and government-funded programmes for higher-voltage GaN above 1000V [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

## Display, infrared and the specialist materials stack

The technical portfolio extended beyond the better-known GaAs, InP and GaN families. IQE’s public materials pointed to continued work in microLED and infrared materials. H1 2024 announced a new 8-inch GaAs and GaN RGB microLED product portfolio with strong engagement from Tier 1 consumer-mobile and display manufacturers [2024 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/2024-interim-results/). The annual report said IQE also maintained a partnership with a leading smart-glasses developer in GaN microLED displays [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). H1 2025 added a customer partnership to develop microLEDs for high-density, power-efficient datacom interconnects [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

Infrared work was equally tangible. The global-footprint page listed substrate lines in GaAs, GaSb, InP, InSb and InAs [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). The 2025 interim results said IQE had delivered first commercial orders for 6-inch GaSb epiwafers for large-area imaging products aimed at space and satellite applications [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

## Development spend and the persistence of the roadmap

The official record also showed that IQE kept funding technology development through the downturn. The FY2023 results said the group maintained a focus on research and development with £2.8m of capitalised technology development [FY 2023 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/full-year-2023-results/). The 2024 annual report highlighted £2m of technology-related development expenditure [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf). IQE’s own corporate description in the 2025 interim results said the company leveraged an intellectual-property portfolio comprising know-how and patents to produce wafers of superior quality, yield and unit economics [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

That mattered because the technical dossier was not merely a catalogue of static products. It was a sequence of funded qualification programmes: InP lasers for AI-linked transceivers, quantum-dot-laser supply-chain build-out, 650V and higher-voltage GaN power, 8-inch microLED platforms, and space-oriented GaSb imaging materials [2024 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/2024-interim-results/) [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf) [2025 Interim Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/2025-interim-results/).

## What the R&D chapter really showed

The primary-source record did not support treating IQE as a generic materials vendor waiting passively for demand to arrive. It supported a narrower and more concrete reading: IQE was running a portfolio of process-development and qualification programmes across multiple compound-semiconductor families, with the most commercially significant emphasis moving toward AI datacom photonics and GaN Power.

That distinction mattered analytically. It meant the technological case for IQE depended less on abstract scientific novelty than on the company’s ability to turn those official qualification milestones into repeat production under the financial constraints described elsewhere in the dossier.

chapters.title: Capacity utilisation, customer concentration, captive-epi competition, capital structure
chapters.body:
## The utilisation trap
