IQE’s cost structure remained defined by its reactor base. Revenue had fallen from £178.0m in 2020 to £115.3m in 2023 before recovering only marginally to £118.0m in 2024 [Summary Financials](https://www.iqep.com/investors/summary-financials/). In a manufacturing model built around specialised, fixed-cost equipment, that was enough to keep gross margin structurally weak.

The near-term mitigant was the same one management kept foregrounding: better absorption from photonics and AI-linked optical demand. IQE’s own market pages made clear that InP, GaAs and GaN all had roles in datacentre optical links and power efficiency [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/). The risk was timing rather than direction.

## Customer concentration and programme dependency

IQE did not publicly map out all major counterparties in the cited filings, but it repeatedly acknowledged dependence on a base of global marquee customers and on a relatively small number of large end programmes [Trading Update and Strategic Review Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/trading-update-and-strategic-review-update/). That left the group exposed to inventory digestion, platform delays and changes in sourcing strategy at the programme level.

The September 2025 trading update captured the mechanism: weak mobile-handset sales, persistent wireless softness and delayed US defence funding all pushed revenue recognition to the right [Trading Update and Strategic Review Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/trading-update-and-strategic-review-update/). A single large programme slipping by two quarters mattered more in this business than it would in a more diversified semiconductor supply model.

## Captive epitaxy as the structural competitor

The merchant model was strongest when customers wanted a specialist partner and weakest when volumes became large enough to justify bringing growth in-house or wrapping it inside a foundry-style platform. IQE’s AI/datacentre thesis implicitly depended on enough optical and power programmes remaining open to merchant supply [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/). If the most attractive markets internalised more of that value chain, the end-market tailwind would not fully translate into IQE revenue.

## Capital structure and liquidity headroom

IQE remained pre-profit at the consolidated level through the contraction period. The group reported adjusted net debt of £18.8m at 31 December 2024 and cash of £4.7m before the March 2025 convertible loan note and April 2026 MACOM package reset the balance sheet [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/) [Closing of CLN Financing](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/closing-of-convertible-loan-note-financing/) [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/). Even after those financings, the business still needed the operating recovery to arrive.

The fixed infrastructure remained heavy. IQE had 479 employees at the end of 2024 and active sites in South Wales, Milton Keynes, North Carolina, Massachusetts, Spokane and Taiwan [IQE Annual Report 2024](https://www.iqep.com/media/q4enmqw3/iqe-annual-report-and-accounts-2024.pdf) [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/). That was a much leaner estate than during the Bethlehem years, but not yet a low-breakeven one.

## AI photonics execution risk

The forward thesis was now closely tied to AI-related communications infrastructure. IQE’s own product and market pages linked InP to 800G cloud infrastructure and GaN to datacentre power systems [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/). That created upside, but it also meant the investment case depended on programme timing outside the company’s control.

A six-month delay in customer qualification or optical-module deployment would still hit IQE asymmetrically because the cost base accrued continuously while revenue remained episodic.

## Substrate supply and process complexity

The product set itself showed why supply risk remained non-trivial. InP, GaAs and GaN each required different structures, wavelengths, substrate options and qualification paths [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/) [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/). Even where end demand strengthened, upstream substrate availability, reactor scheduling and qualification complexity could slow the conversion of demand into recognised revenue.

## The vicious cycle

These risks interacted. Under-utilisation weakened cash generation. Weaker cash generation limited the room for process-development investment, talent retention and selective capacity optimisation. Reduced flexibility then made it harder to win or ramp the very programmes needed to improve utilisation.

The Pennsylvania sale and North Carolina consolidation showed that management was willing to rationalise the footprint [Pennsylvania site sale](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-completion-of-pennsylvania-site-sale-process-as-part-of-global-consolidation-strategy/) [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). The unresolved question was whether that rationalisation, plus the fresh capital raised in 2025 and 2026, had gone far enough to break the cycle before the next downturn tested the balance sheet again.

chapters.title: The InP-photonics-led recovery scenario and the InP-substrate question
chapters.body:
## The InP demand thesis: structure and preconditions

By the time IQE replaced Americo Lemos in October 2024, the recovery thesis had clearly shifted away from the old consumer-VCSEL narrative and toward optical interconnect, AI-linked datacentre growth and a narrower set of higher-value communications and defence programmes [IQE CEO Departure](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2024/iqe-announces-departure-of-chief-executive-officer/) [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/). The company’s own InP materials positioned the platform as part of global fibre networks, hyperscale datacentres, 800G AI infrastructure, cloud services and secure defence systems [InP](https://www.iqep.com/products/inp/).

The structural logic was straightforward. If optical links and power-efficient datacentre architectures scaled, merchant demand for InP, GaAs and GaN should increase alongside them [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/) [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/) [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/). The unresolved question was how much of that increase would reach IQE soon enough to absorb the fixed manufacturing base.

## The InP epi supply chain and IQE's position in it

IQE’s economics were still governed by wafer area shipped and reactor utilisation rather than by end-customer excitement. The company’s January 2026 trading update said H2 2025 photonics demand had been higher than forecast because of continued growth in AI and datacentre markets, and that Q1 2026 order visibility had improved [Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/trading-update/). That was the most direct evidence within the frozen window that the InP thesis was reaching the order book.

## The 5G RF floor: modest recovery, not a second peak

Wireless still mattered, but as a base load rather than a speculative peak story. GaAs remained central to mobile and wireless infrastructure, while the FY 2024 results credited the year-on-year improvement in wireless revenue to stronger Asian penetration and GaN demand for 5G infrastructure [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/) [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). That was supportive, not transformative.

## VCSEL: automotive LiDAR's promise and its present scale

VCSELs did not disappear from the product story, but they were no longer the organising principle of the equity case. IQE’s GaAs page still positioned VCSELs in 3D sensing and optical communications [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/). The problem was one of comparative scale: the recovery narrative now sat with datacentre optical links and GaN power, not with a rerun of the old handset-sensing cycle.

## Operational posture under new leadership

The Meier-Cubitt regime was built around tighter financial discipline. The FY 2024 results highlighted more than 10% headcount reduction, an 8% cut in adjusted SG&A, the completed Pennsylvania-to-North Carolina MBE consolidation, and the start of the South Wales consolidation into Newport [FY 2024 Results](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/full-year-2024-results/). The recovery case therefore required not just end-demand improvement, but proof that the smaller footprint could convert incremental revenue into visibly better cash generation.

## Capital structure: the liquidity constraint

The balance-sheet pressure that dominated 2024 was materially eased, first by the £18m zero-coupon convertible loan note raised in March 2025 and then by the £81m MACOM-led package announced in April 2026 [Closing of CLN Financing](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2025/closing-of-convertible-loan-note-financing/) [Strategic Review Conclusion](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/conclusion-of-strategic-review/). The capital constraint was not gone, but it was no longer the immediate existential issue it had been.

## Risks in the recovery scenario

| Risk factor | Mechanism | Current read |
|---|---|---|
| Capacity utilisation | Incremental revenue still had to absorb a specialised fixed-cost base | Improved, but not yet resolved |
| Programme concentration | A relatively small number of large wireless, photonics and defence programmes drove results | Structural feature of the model |
| Captive or platform integration | More value could be internalised by integrated or foundry-style customers | Persistent medium-term risk |
| Capital structure | Fresh funding bought time, not immunity from another downturn | Substantially improved after 2025–2026 financings |
| InP and process bottlenecks | Qualification timing and upstream complexity could slow conversion of demand into sales | Industry-wide constraint |

## The central question

The chapter’s analytical core therefore remained a single question: would the AI/datacentre optical build-out translate into merchant InP revenue at a scale sufficient to cover IQE’s fixed cost base and restore structural profitability?

The constructive case was not hard to state. The company had a broad active footprint, a product line that explicitly targeted AI and datacentre applications, and improving photonics demand by the start of 2026 [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/) [AI and Datacentres](https://www.iqep.com/markets/ai-and-datacentres/) [Trading Update](https://www.iqep.com/media/press-releases/2026/trading-update/). The bearish case was equally straightforward: utilisation had disappointed for years, and even after two financing events the group still needed real operating leverage, not just better narrative alignment.

As of 23 May 2026, the thesis had not yet been resolved. The equipment was in place, the balance sheet had been stabilised, and the demand signal had strengthened. What remained unproven was the speed at which those three facts would converge in the reported numbers.

## Appendix C — Product and Material System Categories

**Gallium arsenide (GaAs):** Mobile, Wi-Fi and wireless infrastructure, optical communications, 3D sensing and display applications [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/).

**Gallium nitride (GaN):** 5G base stations, radar, satellite communications, EV power electronics, datacentre power management and microLED applications [GaN](https://www.iqep.com/products/gan/).

**VCSEL epi structures:** 3D sensing and optical-communications use cases described within the GaAs platform [GaAs](https://www.iqep.com/products/gaas/).

**Substrates and specialist materials:** IQE’s footprint also included substrate production using Cz/LEC and VGF techniques, plus substrate lines in GaAs, GaSb, InP, InSb and InAs [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/).

## Appendix F — Competitive Architecture

**Merchant epitaxy:** Independent wafer growth sold into multiple end markets; this was the model IQE continued to champion [Global footprint](https://www.iqep.com/about-us/sites/).

**Captive integrated manufacturing:** Device manufacturers that internalise epitaxy inside a broader product margin.

**Foundry-integrated specialty flows:** Platform partnerships or foundry processes that capture the epitaxy step inside a wider manufacturing stack.

financials.key_finding: IQE is a structurally important but financially constrained pure-play in compound semiconductor epitaxy. The 2022-2024 period saw revenue compression as the Apple VCSEL volume that drove 2017-2020 growth normalised, while losses persisted on under-utilisation of the Bethlehem and Taunton US facilities. The 2024-2026 thesis is the InP photonics demand inflection from AI data centre optical interconnect plus the recovery in 5G RF.

principal_facilities_floor_area_sq_ft.taunton_ma: Mega-facility — multiple hundred thousand sq ft

structural_observations: IQE serves multiple end markets — RF (smartphone/base station), photonics (datacom/telecom/sensing), power electronics, advanced sensing — each with distinct cycles. The aggregate cyclicality follows these end markets but the company's gross margin is structurally sensitive to facility utilisation given the capital-intensive epi reactors.

The Apple VCSEL story 2017-2020: IQE was a principal epi supplier into Apple's Face ID supply chain via Lumentum and others; the Apple VCSEL volume drove revenue and gross margin in that period. The post-2020 unwind was severe.
Bethlehem PA facility: opened in 2018 as one of the largest compound semiconductor epi facilities globally. Has carried significant idle capacity through 2022-2024.
The CEO transition in October 2024 (Americo Lemos departure) signalled the board's view that the operational restructuring needed accelerated execution.
The InP/photonics opportunity from AI data centre optical interconnect represents the principal forward strategic thesis — 800G, 1.6T transceivers consume substantial InP epi area per unit.
